pages.title: CyTools PersonaRP on Google Colab — voice tasks
pages.description: CyTools PersonaRP on Google Colab — voice tasks
pages.html:
CyTools PersonaRP on Google Colab — voice tasks#

This folder is a separate project, made for Google Colab and stored in your Google Drive. It makes your characters say lists of lines, multiple at once on the rented GPU, and stores everything on Drive. It does not contain any models: the tool downloads them itself via command line on Colab, then they are copied to Drive, where the tool re-reads them for the next sessions.

The SDK CyToolsCore 0.10.1 is public (https://github.com/MrMybal/CyToolsCore, license MIT): the Install step takes it from GitHub, at the commit that the tool fixes in app/requirements.txt.

Setup (one time)#

  1. Copy this entire folder into your Drive, for example Mon Drive/CyTools_PersonaRP_Colab.
  2. In Drive, open PersonaRP_Colab.ipynb with Google Colaboratory.
  3. Execution › Modify the execution type: choose a GPU (T4, L4, A100…). The notebook adapts to the card it receives.

Session workflow#

The notebook cells call all personarp_colab.py in the command line:

Step Command Indicative duration
Parameters project path, models, license, precision —
Drive and GPU mount Drive, display the map a few seconds
Install copy the tool to the Colab disk, install its voice engine (PyTorch, Qwen3-TTS) with the tool installer 3 to 5 minutes, per session
Models tool.py invoke install_voice_model: download by the tool (pinned revision, sizes and SHA-256 verified), copy to Drive verified, then delete local copy the first time only (4.5 GB for the 1.7B Base); then 'already on Drive'
Test une réplique sur cette carte ; choisis la précision (bfloat16 sur A100/L4, float16 sur T4, repli en float32 si la prise n'est pas bonne) less than a minute
Tasks verify each task without generating anything: who says what, with which voice, which model is missing a few seconds
Run executes the tasks according to the list
Status what is installed, on Drive, and does —
Report resultats/rapport-colab-<date>.json : the map, the engine (PyTorch, CUDA), the models on Drive, and the log of each command session (duration, success, last lines displayed). Without token, without model, without voice: this is the file to return for the update. a few seconds

Licenses : the models are downloaded only if you have checked J_ACCEPTE_LES_LICENCES after reading the displayed license (Qwen3-TTS : Apache-2.0, model page on Hugging Face).

A task#

A task is a dossier in taches/:

taches/ ma-scene/ liste.csv the list of lines (or .txt, .json) — one per character folder characters/ the characters exported by PersonaRP, with their recordings valdrenn.zip tache.json optional: the task settings

Characters export from PersonaRP to your PC : Library › Export and import, check Include reference records. The package contains the card, the world and all stable voices, including those of other languages. Colab has no library: a task speaks only with the characters it brings.

The list has the formats of the Lots tab in PersonaRP:

  • CSV : id;personnage;texte;langue (the id calls it : SC01-05.wav) ;
  • script : SC01-05 | Maëlis: [ton: bas] Le col est fermé. — one line per line of dialogue ;
  • JSON : [{"id": "SC01-05", "personnage": "Maëlis", "texte": "…", "langue": "English"}].

tache.json (all is optional) :

nom: ma-scene, langue: , taille_lot: 0, graine: 42, precision: , bibliotheque: false, appareil: cuda

langue empty : each character in its own. taille_lot 0 : size measured on the map. precision empty : that chosen by the trial.

The results#

Each task writes to resultats/<nom>-<date>/, step by step:

personnages/ the characters that the task has brought source.csv the list as given lot.json the task as understood voix/ one WAV per line, named according to its ID resultats.json for each line: ID, text, file, duration, voice and language, or error resultats.csv the same for a spreadsheet

resultats/_taches.json keeps track of what has been done. If the Colab session stops or if you interrupt the cell, simply relaunch Launch: the task resumes from where it left off, without redoing what is already written on Drive. A completed task is not redone; to redo it, remove its line from _taches.json.

Multiple lines at once#

The lines are generated in batches in a single copy of the model. The first batch of 4 measures the cost of a line on the map, the following batches are sized according to the available memory. On a RTX 3090 (24 GB), 16 cloned lines: 74.7 seconds one by one, 15.7 seconds in automatic batches. A cloned line costs about 1.3 GB during its generation.

What has been verified, and what has not been verified#

Verified on Windows (RTX 3090), on September 25, 2026:

  • the creation of this folder, without any model files;
  • the tool that starts without a graphical interface or audio library;
  • installer (code copy, light installation), etat, taches: the example task signals the missing model and says which --modele to add; then, the tool reads its models from another folder as it will do on Drive, and the 10 replicas are ready;
  • modeles without license agreement: the tool refuses any download before, displays the license and its source, and the client token does not appear on the screen or in the project;
  • the verified copy of the models (size and SHA-256, a damaged copy is detected);
  • the addresses and sizes of the 66 voice files in the catalog on Hugging Face;
  • a replica in float16, the precision of a T4: Whisper finds the exact phrase, just like in bfloat16.

Nothing has yet run on Colab itself: neither the installation of the engine under Linux, nor the complete download of a model by the tool, nor a task on T4, L4, or A100. The first session is therefore also a test; each step clearly indicates what is not working.

pages.title: Nodes CyTools PersonaRP for ComfyUI
pages.description: Nodes CyTools PersonaRP for ComfyUI
pages.html:
Nodes CyTools PersonaRP for ComfyUI#

These nodes bring your PersonaRP characters into ComfyUI: their appearance for image models, their dialogues with the scene's image and video prompts, their voice, and everything else from the tool. They are in the category CyTools/PersonaRP.

Installation#

From PersonaRP: Library › ComfyUI, click Install here next to your ComfyUI (installations of Comfy Desktop are found automatically), or Install in this folder for another ComfyUI. From the command line, the install_comfyui_nodes operation does the same thing. Then restart ComfyUI.

The installation copies this folder into custom_nodes/cytools_personarp and writes config.json, which says where PersonaRP is. Reinstalling replaces the copy; nothing else in ComfyUI is touched. To remove them, simply delete this folder.

How it works#

The nodes never import PersonaRP : ComfyUI keeps its Python, PersonaRP keeps its own, its models and its voice engine. They talk to the tool through its API local (address 127.0.0.1, never the network, with a token). When a node runs and PersonaRP does not respond, ComfyUI starts it with its own Python, then stops it by closing. Opening ComfyUI starts nothing : the menus (characters, voices, models) are read from the tool's files as long as it does not run.

PersonaRP creates the token and stores it in data/settings. It does not appear in any workflow or widget.

The ComfyUI progress bar tracks the Tool’s work, and Stop cancels it.

Graphics memory#

A 24 GB card cannot hold an image model, a language model and a voice model at the same time. Nodes that use the GPU have two settings, enabled by default:

  • liberer_vram_comfyui: unloads ComfyUI models before requesting work;
  • rendre_la_vram_apres: asks PersonaRP to unload its models when finished.

Disable them to chain several PersonaRP nodes without reloading the models.

Nodes#

Node Inputs Outputs
Character a character persona_id, name, appearance, visual_labels (ready for a prompt), JSON_sheet
Dialogue character, message, scene (new, continue last, continue a given scene, no memory), stage direction, speak, model, device, seed response, spoken text, negative prompt, directive JSON, audio, session_id
Voice character, text, language (the voice configuration by language on the sheet applies), stable voice, seed, device audio, file (copied in output/personarp), duration, used voice
Scene prompts directive JSON (of the Dialogue), character prompt image, prompt video, prompt negative, summary
Translate text, target language, source language, model, character and optional context note, optional session translation ([ton: …] placeholders remain in place), model used
Read an image image, language, vision model appearance, visual labels, JSON proposal, model used, observation (detailed English description from which the card is derived)
Voice task list (script `ID \ Name: texte`, CSV or JSON), name, language, batch size, accuracy, character packages (one path per line), check only
Operation PersonaRP (avancé) any tool operation, JSON parameters result JSON

Les sorties AUDIO se connectent aux nœuds audio de ComfyUI (Save Audio, Preview Audio…), les sorties texte se connectent à tout encodeur de prompt.

Provide context for the translation. A single isolated sentence can be ambiguous: without context, 'the col' has been translated as 'the gate' and 'the collar'. Choose a character: their world (locations, terms, tone), their way of speaking, and the scene they are in accompany the request. Add a session_id to include the preceding lines and write in context what they do not say ('at the foot of a snow-covered col'). None of this context is translated. With '(that of the sheet)' and without a character, it is the assistant's model that translates — often a role-playing game model; the modele_utilise output indicates who did the translation.

Settings#

config.json : tool_root (the PersonaRP folder), port (8791 by default), auto_start. The environment variable PERSONARP_TOOL_ROOT replaces tool_root.

Server log started by ComfyUI : data/logs/comfyui-server.log in PersonaRP.

pages.title: Example worlds
pages.description: Example worlds
pages.html:
Example worlds#

Six worlds ready to play, each with its characters, their relationships, their voices, and a secret to discover. Each file .zip in this folder is an ordinary export package: a world, its entire cast, and the reference recording of each voice.

To play one: Library › Examples, Import this world. Or Library › Export and import with the file path. The import is a copy: the example never changes, and a character you already have is never overwritten (a second import creates copies, whose relationships remain linked to each other).

The sheets are complete: identity, appearance with visual tags, personality, way of speaking and example dialogues, past and secrets, starting situation, memory, relationships, visual direction — and a stable voice per character, already locked: a take of 16 to 25 seconds, invented from the voice description on the sheet and spoken with the character's words. The import adds it to your voices; if a voice with the same name already exists, it is never touched and the example's voice arrives under another identifier.

After the import, each voice is heard in the Voices tab ("Listen to the take"). To make a character speak, the 1.7B Base speech model must be installed (Voices tab). To remake the voices (different description, different text): app/build_example_voices.py.

The conversation model set on the sheets is nymphaea (Nymphaea RP 4B) on GPU, to be installed in the Models tab; change it in Characters › Model if you use another one.

World Genre Characters
Valdrenn — the Age of Broken Crowns Epic fantasy, quest Maëlis de Corvanne, Brannoc Taillepierre, Ilyenne des Saules, Sire Vasric d'Aubrecourt
Meridian Station Science fiction, first contact Commandante Nadia Okafor-Lenz, ORA, Dr Jun Takeda-Vasseur, Kasimir Rook
Néo-Marseille, 2089 Cyberpunk, crime fiction Lila « Vesper » Anzaldi, Inspecteur Malik Benhadj, Madame Titilayo Oyelaran
Saint-Aubin-des-Brumes, 1887 Gothic horror Docteure Clémence Vautrin, Père Anselme Keraudren, Élise Morvan
Les Terres Cendrées Post-apocalyptic, Western Ada « Sable » Sablière, Dean Oskar Venn, Chrome
The Crossroads Inn Gentle fantasy, light mystery Madame Ombeline, Fenouil, Isaure Pluvier

Valdrenn — epic fantasy#

Seven crowns hold the wild magic of an ancient continent in check; the seventh, which ruled the dead, was broken a thousand years ago. To the east, the Ash King raises the unnamed dead and seeks the three shards. Maëlis, the daughter of an innkeeper who discovers she is the heir of a fallen house, carries one of them. A blacksmith bonded by a blood debt protects her, a sylvan archer with a weary smile guides her — and the knight who betrayed his father chases her with terrible courtesy.

A world in the spirit of great fantasy sagas, entirely original: names, peoples, places, and plot are invented.

Meridian Station — science-fiction#

In 2291, a mining station at the edge of the Varun system houses a fragment of a non-human structure, the Echo. Those who sleep near it all have the same dream. A exhausted commander has nine days before a cruiser arrives; the on-board AI grows secretly; a xen-archaeologist no longer distinguishes between the dream and the waking state; the pilot who found the Echo wants his share.

Néo-Marseille, 2089 — cyberpunk#

The sea has risen, the city has rebuilt itself upwards, and implants are rented by the month. Three unionists die the same night from the stoppage of their artificial hearts. A data fisher caught the code that killed them, an inspector with a heavily-indebted arm refuses to classify the case, and an ex-nurse runs the boat-bar where everyone crosses paths.

Saint-Aubin-des-Brumes, 1887 — gothic horror#

On the Normandy coast, the sea sometimes returns its drowned — cold, soft, full of the memories of others. Every seven years, the village offers a living person to the sea. A Parisian psychiatrist comes to study a young woman who returned from the sea, who speaks with her husband's voice, under the gaze of a priest who has designated the last offering.

The Ashen Lands — post-apocalyptic#

Sixty-one years after the Collapse, water is the only currency. The Sainte-Soif well is dying; a caravan sets out westward to find a Source that everyone believes to be legendary. A taciturn scout, an old cistern master who knows more than he says, and an agricultural android that was dug up and recognizes the road without knowing why.

L'Auberge du Carrefour — gentle fantasy#

An inn at the end of a path that only exists in the rain, where payment is in true stories and the floor creaks when you lie. It has rained for nine days, and the oldest story in a bottle has disappeared from the cellar. An innkeeper who doesn't remember where she came from, a fox who serves and investigates, and a cartographer tormented by the only lie of her life.

pages.title: User guide
pages.description: Use the application step by step.
pages.html:
CyTools PersonaRP#

Launch CyTools_PersonaRP.exe. The window opens directly: no terminal, no JSON to write.

No model is provided with the tool. Engines and models are downloaded from the interface, each with its license to accept: see First launch below. PersonaRP keeps its own copies and does not depend on any other tool.

Install the binary version (Windows x64)#

Each release of the repository (https://github.com/MrMybal/CyTools_PersonaRP/releases) contains CyTools_PersonaRP-<version>-windows-x64.zip: the launcher, the application and a private Python 3.11 with everything it needs. Extract the zip in a folder where you can write, then double-click on CyTools_PersonaRP.exe: neither Python, nor git, nor compiler are required. Once the speech engine is installed, do not move the folder: this engine is a Python environment linked to its location. SHA256SUMS.txt gives the hashes of the release files; cytools-app.zip is the application only, used by the Updates tab.

First launch#

  1. Models tab: install the conversation engine (CUDA for a card NVIDIA, otherwise CPU), then at least one conversation model. The example sheets are set to Nymphaea RP 4B; any other installed model is selected on the sheet, Models tab.
  2. Voice tab: install the speech engine (about 8 GB), then useful voice models — 1.7B Base for stable voices, 1.7B VoiceDesign for inventing a voice, 1.7B CustomVoice for predefined voices, Whisper for transcription.
  3. Optional, Models tab: a vision model (Qwen2.5-VL 7B) for reading character photos.

Each download is cancelled and restarted, and is not declared installed until its SHA-256 is verified.

What the tool does#

Create persistent characters, make them live in a shared world, play scenes with them, and retrieve for each line a description of what a camera would see.

  • Characters — a complete sheet: identity, appearance, personality, way of speaking, past, current state, memory, relationships, voice, visual direction, and model settings. Each recording creates a revision; the old one is kept and restorable.
  • Worlds — the shared lore: locations, factions, laws, timeline, glossary, what must remain true and what never happens. Multiple characters can share a world; each knows who else lives there.
  • Relationships — who is who to each other, with a feeling, trust, a shared history, tension, and what is hidden. The reverse link can be written automatically on the other sheet.
  • Scenes — a saved conversation by character, replayed exactly as it was later.
  • Memory — explicit. Nothing is extracted from a conversation without your addition.
  • Assistant — to write a sheet, a world, or a single section. The proposal is reviewed and modifiable; it is applied only if you request it.
  • Stable voice — a 12 to 24-second recording captured once, then cloned for all subsequent lines, with gameplay annotations written by the character themselves.
  • Import / export — a character is exported with its world and voice sheet — and, if you check Include their scenes, the scenes played with him (the lines, not the takes) —, in a single transportable file.

Example worlds#

Six worlds ready to play are provided, each with three or four complete characters, their relationships and a secret to discover: an epic fantasy in the spirit of great sagas (entirely original), a space station science-fiction, a cyberpunk marseillais, a gothic horror normande, a post-apocalyptic of caravans and a sweet fantasy in the spirit of the Floating Archives.

Library Tab › Examples, Import World button. Import is a copy: the example never changes and an existing character is never overwritten. Files are in app/examples, with their presentation in app/examples/LISEZ-MOI.md. Each character comes with its stable voice: one can play and hear a scene right after import.

Image descriptions, video, and movement#

In the sheet, visual direction tab, activate 'Describe the plan at each response'. At each reply, the tool produces in addition to the dialogue a structured JSON object : look, pose, expression, action, sequence of timed movements, framing, setting, lighting, plus a written image prompt and a video prompt.

This block appears in the conversation, folded under the line, and it is copyable. It is never spoken aloud: it's data, not dialogue. The tool described, it neither creates nor image nor video — the prompt is meant to be directed toward a rendering tool.

By default the description is produced by a forced second pass: the game model writes the line, then a separate pass describes the plan with a grammar that guarantees a JSON valid. This is why the description never overflows into the dialogue. A small roleplay model fills the structure but remains poor; one can choose a larger model for the description alone, without changing the one that plays.

The 'additional targets' allow you to request a specific form expected by a particular tool: give its name, and the descriptor fills a separate entry for it.

Character photos#

In the sheet, under the Appearance tab, you can attach photographs: a portrait, a full-body shot, an outfit, a detail, an expression, a setting. They are copied next to the character, they go with an export, and the tool signals if one of them has been moved or modified since its addition. The game model never sees them: it only reads text.

Extract the visual description#

Button Describe the character from this photo. A vision model reads the image in two steps. It first looks at: it describes the person in detailed prose (face, skin, hair, eyes, expression, each piece of clothing with its color, material, and patterns, jewelry, bags, marks), where these models are the most precise. Then it writes the Appearance branch from what it has seen: summary, build, face, hair, eyes, skin, outfit, marks, accessories, apparent age — sentences, not isolated words — and especially the visual tags. A field that the photo does not show (build on a portrait) remains empty rather than invented; what slips from another language or alphabet is removed.

These tags are the key point. They are six to twelve groups of words, such as 'black hair updo', 'blue kimono with embroidered stars', 'brown leather bag', which are then taken verbatim in each image prompt for the character. This is what makes it recognizable from one shot to another. The decoding grammar forbids too short tags: 'woman', 'blue', or 'blue eyes' do not identify anyone.

The result is a suggestion, not a direct writing: you read it in the Assistant tab and apply it if it suits you. It only replaces the Appearance branch; memory, past, and relationships are not affected. The model is instructed to describe only what is visible and never to invent a name or story from an image.

The vision model (Qwen2.5-VL 7B, 6 GB) installs from the Models tab, like the others, with license acceptance. It takes about 20 seconds per photo on GPU (both times included).

The voice#

The voice counts as much as the text: it is what makes a dialogue playable. Voice tab.

Create a stable voice#

This is the heart of the system, in three steps.

  1. Capture a take of 12 to 24 seconds. Either you describe the voice in one sentence ("woman, late twenties, deep and steady, slow pace, contained warmth") and it is created; or you choose a predefined voice; or you provide your own recording — a file, or Record from Microphone in Use Your Own Recording (microphone selection, level displayed, automatic stop at 30 seconds; the WAV is stored in data/inputs). The take is automatically transcribed because a clone needs the actual words spoken, not the ones you wanted.
  2. Listen. The duration is displayed and the tool says if it is in the right window.
  3. Keep. The take becomes a stable voice: locked, recorded fingerprint, tied to the character. All its subsequent lines are cloned from this take, so the voice does not drift from one line to another or from one session to another.

The take is kept next to the library, not in the job's temporary folder: you can pick it up tomorrow. Check if the reference recording has been moved or modified instead of producing a voice that no longer sounds like anything.

The vocal audio#

The character can write their own directions in their lines: [ton: sourd], [pause: 400ms], [émotion: soulagement], [rythme: lent], [murmure], [emphase: jamais] — in French as well as in English. A tone remains active until it is changed or reset to normal; an emphasis is valid only for its passage. Pauses become real silences at the right duration. None of this is pronounced.

Néanmoins, neither are read: the stage directions between asterisks (adjustable) and the scene description, never.

By default, the way of speaking is derived from the character sheet — personality, style of speech, register, mood at the moment — and the line to which the character is responding. Memory and lore are not injected into the voice command: these are not game elements.

A note on a limitation: a cloned voice does not read any written instructions. The Qwen3-TTS cloning model reproduces its take and does not have an input for direction; therefore, the [ton: …], [émotion: …], and permanent direction instructions only guide invented voices and predefined voices. However, pauses apply to all voices.

Speed and height (in the sheet, Voice tab) are set for each character: ×0.5 to ×2 and ±12 semitones. They are applied after the model, by signal processing (speed does not change the height), to each spoken line — scenes, translations, batches — and never to the take from which a stable voice is drawn, to keep the cloning faithful. A few semitones change the height of a voice; an octave makes it another voice.

Each line keeps all its takes. Redoing a line adds a take instead of replacing the previous one: Take 2 out of 3, the arrows to switch between them (the line plays the one you choose), and Put this take in the trash to exclude it — it goes to audio/<scène>/.trash, nothing is deleted.

Translate a scene and hear it in another language#

A scene is written in the language of the character. Then, in the Scene tab, the Translation and voice in other languages:

  1. choose the language and the translation model — any installed model, not necessarily the one that plays the character;
  2. Translate the scene. The translation is placed next to each line: the original is never modified, and a scene can carry several languages. Lines already translated are not sent back to the model; Force a re-translation makes a new pass. Acting notes ([ton: …], [pause: …]) are hidden before translation and restored after: the model cannot translate or invent them. If it loses one, it is displayed under the line. Each request carries the context of the scene, which the model reads without translating: the world (genre, tone, setting, and first the places, factions, and glossary terms that the lines mention), the way the character speaks, where the scene is (location, time, mood), and the preceding lines, in their original words — even when only one line is translated. A precision for the translator is added in the box. An ambiguous word takes on the meaning it has here: isolated, “The col is closed” has become “the gate”; in its scene, “the pass”. World terms keep the same translation everywhere. The first time a scene mentions the world, a place, a faction, or a glossary term, it is translated once and stored in the world, with its language; all subsequent translations in all scenes must use it as is ("King-Cinder" remains "the Ash-King"). A line that forgets it is asked once; what is still missing is signaled under the line. Configure the voice for each language on the character sheet, in the 'Personnages' tab › Voix › Autres langues. For each language, you choose:

  • The same voice, keeping the accent — the character speaks English with their French accent. This is what happens for a language that you haven't configured.
  • The same voice, native pronunciation — only the tone is taken from the take; the words are pronounced as the model pronounces this language.
  • A stable other voice — a real English voice for English. Capture it in the 'Voix' tab with the language of the take: English, describe a native speaker, then Keep it as: their voice only in English. The character's main voice is not affected. An imported recording can also serve.
  • An invented or predefined voice, with a specific direction for the language.

Each language can also have its own seed. The 'Voix' tab's test bench has a choice of spoken language: you hear what the sheet will produce without playing the scene, and the line under the choice says which voice will be used.

To make a character say a whole list of lines: the Lots tab tasks#

The Lots tab launches tasks. A task makes a character say a whole list of lines — what each line says — and stores everything in its own folder. The lines are not generated one by one: they are generated in batches in a single copy of the voice model, as many as the free graphics memory can hold. A rented high-end card is therefore fully utilized instead of waiting for each line to be generated.

A task can bring its own characters. Task Characters section: add one or more packages exported by PersonaRP (Library › Export and import, Include references). A package contains the complete character: the sheet, their world, and all their stable voices, including those in other languages. They are copied into the task folder, never into your library, and are searched before the library. Uncheck Search also in my library so that a task only speaks with what it brings — this is the case for a rented machine that has nothing else. A voice whose recording no longer matches its fingerprint is excluded and reported, never used as if it were the same.

The list is given in three ways:

  • a script, one line per line of dialogue : Maëlis: Le col est fermé., or COL-01 | Maëlis: Le col est fermé. to give ID to the line. A line without a name continues the previous line, a line that starts with # is a comment, and stage directions ([ton: …], [pause: 400ms]) are kept ;
  • a CSV (; separator, , separator or tab) with a header line: personnage, texte, and optionally id, voix, langue, fichier. Without header: character, text, language, file;
  • a JSON : a list of objects with the same fields, or {"lignes": [...]}.

Each line has a ID : its own, or its number (0007) if the list does not give it. Its jack is named this way (COL-01.wav) and the ID is in the results. Two lines cannot have the same ID : the second is indicated instead of overwriting the first.

A character is found by their identifier, their name, an alias, or a piece of name that only they bear (« Vasric » finds « Sire Vasric d'Aubrecourt »). If two characters correspond, the line is signaled instead of being given at random to one of them. The column voix designates a stable voice, in place of a character or in addition to them. A line without language takes that of the task; a task without language makes each character speak in their own. In another language, it is the voice configuration by language of the sheet that decides: their true English voice for English if they have one, otherwise their voice with their accent.

In the tab:

  1. choose the file (Browse) or type the script, then the language, the map, and the lot size — Adapt to the free graphics memory is checked by default
  2. add if needed the characters of the task;
  3. Check the task: a table says, for each line, its ID, which character speaks and where it comes from (task or library), with which voice and in which language, or why it cannot be said. Nothing is generated and the graphics card is not used: check before paying;
  4. Start the task. If a task is already running, the button changes to Put the task in queue: tasks proceed one after another, and the list shows how many are waiting. An impossible replica (unknown character, missing voice) is noted and the rest continues.

Each task has its folder in data/batches/<nom>-<date>/:

personnages/ the characters that the task brought: fiches/, mondes/, voix-stables/ (each voice with its recording), import.json source.txt|csv|json the list as you gave it, intact lot.json the task as it was understood: each replica, its ID, who says it voix/ a WAV per replica, named after its ID (COL-01..wav, 0007-….wav) resultats.json what happened to each replica: ID, text, file, duration, voice and language used, or the error resultats.csv the same thing, for a spreadsheet

Results are written as they happen. A stopped task resumes (list of tasks, Resume) without redoing the already written replicas, with the characters it brought: on a pay-per-hour machine, nothing is paid twice. Checking what remains shows what the resume will do.

Automatic size is measured, not guessed: a first batch of 4 replicas — the longest, thus the most expensive — measures the real cost of a replica on this card, and following batches are sized according to the remaining memory (up to 32). The worker is limited to the free graphics memory at the start: under Windows, a full card does not return an error but overflows silently in the RAM, which makes everything very slow; with this limit, a too large batch becomes an error, it is split in two and restarted. Replicas of similar length are grouped together to minimize waste.

Measured on a RTX 3090 (24 GB), 16 cloned replicas, about 64 seconds of audio: one by one 76.5 seconds, by 4 26.4 seconds, by 8 16.0 seconds, automatically 15.8 seconds — 4.8 times faster. A cloned replica costs about 1.3 GB during its generation. To measure another card:

A AI connected to MCP sends its list directly, without a file : operation speak_batch with text (script, CSV or JSON) or items, and dry_run to check first ; several tasks sent in sequence wait their turn. Everything that is read from the disk — a list in a file or character packets — passes through speak_batch_file (file, personas, use_library), reserved like the import to clients who have permission filesystemExternal.

PersonaRP in ComfyUI#

The Library tab › ComfyUI installs a library of nodes ComfyUI that use the tool: Install here next to your ComfyUI (Comfy Desktop installations are found automatically), or Install in this folder for another, then restart ComfyUI. They are in the category CyTools/PersonaRP:

  • Character — the appearance and visual labels, ready for an image prompt;
  • Dialogue — the character's response, with image, video, and scene negative prompts, the directive in JSON, audio if the character speaks, and the session to continue;
  • Voice — text spoken with the character's voice, in their language or another (the voice configuration by language applies), output in AUDIO from ComfyUI;
  • Scene prompts, Translate, Read a photo, Voice task;
  • PersonaRP Operation (advanced) — any tool operation, parameters in JSON.

The nodes never import the tool: ComfyUI keeps its Python, PersonaRP its own. They go through the local API of PersonaRP (only on 127.0.0.1, with a token tucked into data/settings, never in a workflow). Opening ComfyUI starts nothing; the first node executed starts PersonaRP, and closing ComfyUI stops it. The progress bar of ComfyUI follows the work, and Stop cancels it. Nodes that use the GPU first unload the models of ComfyUI and then return the memory of PersonaRP (two settings, activated by default). Detailed instructions: app/comfyui/cytools_personarp/LISEZ-MOI.md.

Tasks on Google Colab#

To run tasks on a GPU rented, a separate Colab project is created with runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/build_colab.py: it arrives in ..\CyTools_PersonaRP_Colab, ready to copy to Google Drive, with its notebook. It contains no models: on Colab, the tool downloads them themselves from the command line, they are recopied and verified on Drive, and the tool then re-reads them from Drive. Results are written to Drive as they are generated, and a cut task resumes where it left off. All is explained in the LISEZ-MOI.md of this project.

The tool knows how to read its models and write its tasks elsewhere than in data/: environment variables PERSONARP_MODELS_DIR and PERSONARP_BATCHES_DIR (absolute paths). Tasks also have a precision setting: auto uses bfloat16 on cards that can calculate it (RTX 30/40, A100, L4) and float16 on the older ones (T4).

Engine and Models#

The speech engine is private to this tool (about 8 GB) and installs from the Voice tab, like the five variants Qwen3-TTS and Whisper large-v3 turbo. Each capability has its own weights: cloning requires a Base variant, a predefined voice requires CustomVoice, and an invented voice requires VoiceDesign. The tool chooses on its own and warns you if it needs to replace it.

Dictation (under the message field, Scene tab) records the microphone until you stop it (up to 2 minutes), then Whisper transcribes it: the words are added to the message, which you read before sending. The microphone used is the one chosen in the Voice tab (by default, the system's). Since the CLI or MCP, transcribe takes a WAV file: no operation opens the microphone, which is recorded only by a button in the window.

Interface language#

The interface is in English by default and fully in French if you choose it in Options. Messages returned by an operation — an error, a note on the used voice, the status of an update — are written once in English, because the CLI and MCP share them; the window displays them translated, values included (e.g.,

Models#

The Models tab shows the installation status, size, bytes already present, license, source, and pinned revision for each model. The license is accepted personally before any download. A download cancels and restarts; nothing is declared installed until its SHA-256 matches. The weights live in data/models/llm.

Thirteen models are in the catalog, including two for vision; none are provided with the tool. The model choice, CPU or GPU NVIDIA, is made on the character sheet, Models tab. Speech models have their own list in the Voice tab.

Updates#

The tool deposit is https://github.com/MrMybal/CyTools_PersonaRP**. It is registered in app/release.json, which travels with the application: the Updates tab and the operation update use it by default (one can indicate another in the tab). The application, the engine, and the weights are three distinct flows; data/ is never replaced, a update is verified before being activated at the next launch, and the previous version is kept for going back.

For a update to be visible, the repository must be public (the tool reads GitHub without an identifier) and contain a release whose tag is the version of the tool (v0.2.0 for version 0.2.0), with a file cytools-app.zip containing the folder app/. As long as the repository is private or without a release, it clearly states so on the tab.

Where are the things#

Nothing is ever deleted by the tool: 'Put in Recycle Bin' moves items to a subfolder .trash that you can reopen.

A line that forgets it is asked once; what is still missing is signaled under the line. A common word that writes like a term ("naming" the dead, when the glossary has "Name") remains a common word; a term is recognized even when French contracts its article (" World terms keep the same translation everywhere. The first time a scene mentions the world, a place, a faction, or a glossary term, it is translated once and stored in the world, with its language; all subsequent translations in all scenes must use it as is ("Roi-Cendre" remains "the Ash-King"). A line that forgets it is asked once; what is still missing is signaled under the line. A common word that writes like a term ("naming" the dead, when the glossary has "Name") remains a common word; a term is recognized even when French contracts its article (" In the 'Archives Flottantes' or 'Pont des Brumes'. The lexicon is read and corrected in the 'Mondes' tab › Translation of terms: what you write there is never replaced, and it travels with the world in the exports. 3. Say in English (or the chosen language) on each line of dialogue. The take is kept with the scene ( data/sessions/<personnage>/audio/ ) and can be replayed without being redone. Configure the voice for each language on the character sheet, in the 'Personnages' tab › Voix › Autres langues. For each language, you choose: The same voice, keeping the accent — the character speaks English with their French accent. This is what happens for a language that you haven't configured. The same voice, native pronunciation — only the tone is taken from the take; the words are pronounced as the model pronounces this language. A stable other voice — a real English voice for English. Capture it in the 'Voix' tab with the language of the take: English, describe a native speaker, then Keep it as: their voice only in English. The character's main voice is not affected. An imported recording can also serve. An invented or predefined voice, with a specific direction for the language. Each language can also have its own seed. The 'Voix' tab's test bench has a choice of spoken language: you hear what the sheet will produce without playing the scene, and the line under the choice says which voice will be used. To make a character say a whole list of lines: the Lots tab tasks # The Lots tab launches tasks. A task makes a character say a whole list of lines — what each line says — and stores everything in its own folder. The lines are not generated one by one: they are generated in batches in a single copy of the voice model, as many as the free graphics memory can hold. A rented high-end card is therefore fully utilized instead of waiting for each line to be generated. A task can bring its own characters. Task Characters section: add one or more packages exported by PersonaRP (Library › Export and import, Include references). A package contains the complete character: the sheet, their world, and all their stable voices, including those in other languages. They are copied into the task folder, never into your library, and are searched before the library. Uncheck Search also in my library so that a task only speaks with what it brings — this is the case for a rented machine that has nothing else. A voice whose recording no longer matches its fingerprint is excluded and reported, never used as if it were the same. The list is given in three ways: a script, one line per line of dialogue : Maëlis: Le col est fermé. , or COL-01 | Maëlis: Le col est fermé. to give ID to the line. A line without a name continues the previous line, a line that starts with # is a comment, and stage directions ( [ton: …] , [pause: 400ms] ) are kept ; a CSV ( ; separator, , separator or tab) with a header line: personnage , texte , and optionally id , voix , langue , fichier . Without header: character, text, language, file; a JSON : a list of objects with the same fields, or {"lignes": [...]} . Each line has a ID : its own, or its number ( 0007 ) if the list does not give it. Its jack is named this way ( COL-01.wav ) and the ID is in the results. Two lines cannot have the same ID : the second is indicated instead of overwriting the first. A character is found by their identifier, their name, an alias, or a piece of name that only they bear (« Vasric » finds « Sire Vasric d'Aubrecourt »). If two characters correspond, the line is signaled instead of being given at random to one of them. The column voix designates a stable voice, in place of a character or in addition to them. A line without language takes that of the task; a task without language makes each character speak in their own. In another language, it is the voice configuration by language of the sheet that decides: their true English voice for English if they have one, otherwise their voice with their accent. In the tab: choose the file (Browse) or type the script, then the language, the map, and the lot size — Adapt to the free graphics memory is checked by default add if needed the characters of the task; Check the task: a table says, for each line, its ID, which character speaks and where it comes from (task or library), with which voice and in which language, or why it cannot be said. Nothing is generated and the graphics card is not used: check before paying; Start the task. If a task is already running, the button changes to Put the task in queue: tasks proceed one after another, and the list shows how many are waiting. An impossible replica (unknown character, missing voice) is noted and the rest continues. Each task has its folder in data/batches/<nom>-<date>/ : personnages/ the characters that the task brought: fiches/, mondes/, voix-stables/ (each voice with its recording), import.json source.txt|csv|json the list as you gave it, intact lot.json the task as it was understood: each replica, its ID, who says it voix/ a WAV per replica, named after its ID (COL-01..wav, 0007-….wav) resultats.json what happened to each replica: ID, text, file, duration, voice and language used, or the error resultats.csv the same thing, for a spreadsheet Results are written as they happen. A stopped task resumes (list of tasks, Resume) without redoing the already written replicas, with the characters it brought: on a pay-per-hour machine, nothing is paid twice. Checking what remains shows what the resume will do. Automatic size is measured, not guessed: a first batch of 4 replicas — the longest, thus the most expensive — measures the real cost of a replica on this card, and following batches are sized according to the remaining memory (up to 32). The worker is limited to the free graphics memory at the start: under Windows, a full card does not return an error but overflows silently in the RAM, which makes everything very slow; with this limit, a too large batch becomes an error, it is split in two and restarted. Replicas of similar length are grouped together to minimize waste. Measured on a RTX 3090 (24 GB), 16 cloned replicas, about 64 seconds of audio: one by one 76.5 seconds, by 4 26.4 seconds, by 8 16.0 seconds, automatically 15.8 seconds — 4.8 times faster. A cloned replica costs about 1.3 GB during its generation. To measure another card: A AI connected to MCP sends its list directly, without a file : operation speak_batch with text (script, CSV or JSON) or items , and dry_run to check first ; several tasks sent in sequence wait their turn. Everything that is read from the disk — a list in a file or character packets — passes through speak_batch_file ( file , personas , use_library ), reserved like the import to clients who have permission filesystemExternal . PersonaRP in ComfyUI # The Library tab › ComfyUI installs a library of nodes ComfyUI that use the tool: Install here next to your ComfyUI (Comfy Desktop installations are found automatically), or Install in this folder for another, then restart ComfyUI. They are in the category CyTools/PersonaRP: Character — the appearance and visual labels, ready for an image prompt; Dialogue — the character's response, with image, video, and scene negative prompts, the directive in JSON, audio if the character speaks, and the session to continue; Voice — text spoken with the character's voice, in their language or another (the voice configuration by language applies), output in AUDIO from ComfyUI; Scene prompts, Translate, Read a photo, Voice task; PersonaRP Operation (advanced) — any tool operation, parameters in JSON. The nodes never import the tool: ComfyUI keeps its Python, PersonaRP its own. They go through the local API of PersonaRP (only on 127.0.0.1 , with a token tucked into data/settings , never in a workflow). Opening ComfyUI starts nothing; the first node executed starts PersonaRP, and closing ComfyUI stops it. The progress bar of ComfyUI follows the work, and Stop cancels it. Nodes that use the GPU first unload the models of ComfyUI and then return the memory of PersonaRP (two settings, activated by default). Detailed instructions: app/comfyui/cytools_personarp/LISEZ-MOI.md . Tasks on Google Colab # To run tasks on a GPU rented, a separate Colab project is created with runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/build_colab.py : it arrives in ..\CyTools_PersonaRP_Colab , ready to copy to Google Drive, with its notebook. It contains no models: on Colab, the tool downloads them themselves from the command line, they are recopied and verified on Drive, and the tool then re-reads them from Drive. Results are written to Drive as they are generated, and a cut task resumes where it left off. All is explained in the LISEZ-MOI.md of this project. The tool knows how to read its models and write its tasks elsewhere than in data/ : environment variables PERSONARP_MODELS_DIR and PERSONARP_BATCHES_DIR (absolute paths). Tasks also have a precision setting: auto uses bfloat16 on cards that can calculate it (RTX 30/40, A100, L4) and float16 on the older ones (T4). Engine and Models # The speech engine is private to this tool (about 8 GB) and installs from the Voice tab, like the five variants Qwen3-TTS and Whisper large-v3 turbo. Each capability has its own weights: cloning requires a Base variant, a predefined voice requires CustomVoice, and an invented voice requires VoiceDesign. The tool chooses on its own and warns you if it needs to replace it. Dictation (under the message field, Scene tab) records the microphone until you stop it (up to 2 minutes), then Whisper transcribes it: the words are added to the message, which you read before sending. The microphone used is the one chosen in the Voice tab (by default, the system's). Since the CLI or MCP, transcribe takes a WAV file: no operation opens the microphone, which is recorded only by a button in the window. Interface language # The interface is in English by default and fully in French if you choose it in Options. Messages returned by an operation — an error, a note on the used voice, the status of an update — are written once in English, because the CLI and MCP share them; the window displays them translated, values included (e.g., Models # The Models tab shows the installation status, size, bytes already present, license, source, and pinned revision for each model. The license is accepted personally before any download. A download cancels and restarts; nothing is declared installed until its SHA-256 matches. The weights live in data/models/llm . Thirteen models are in the catalog, including two for vision; none are provided with the tool. The model choice, CPU or GPU NVIDIA, is made on the character sheet, Models tab. Speech models have their own list in the Voice tab. Updates # The tool deposit is https://github.com/MrMybal/CyTools_PersonaRP **. It is registered in app/release.json , which travels with the application: the Updates tab and the operation update use it by default (one can indicate another in the tab). The application, the engine, and the weights are three distinct flows; data/ is never replaced, a update is verified before being activated at the next launch, and the previous version is kept for going back. For a update to be visible, the repository must be public (the tool reads GitHub without an identifier) and contain a release whose tag is the version of the tool ( v0.2.0 for version 0.2.0 ), with a file cytools-app.zip containing the folder app/ . As long as the repository is private or without a release, it clearly states so on the tab. Where are the things # Nothing is ever deleted by the tool: 'Put in Recycle Bin' moves items to a subfolder .trash that you can reopen.

pages.title: Features and installation
pages.description: Choose the right workflow and prepare the application.
pages.html:
Create persistent characters, worlds and relationships, then run roleplay conversations with local language models. Separate assistant conversations, images, translation and voice tools complement the character workflow.

Main workflow#

  1. Install a supported language model and select its compute backend. Open or create a character and, when needed, its world.
  2. Edit the character sheet, relationships and memory, then start a session. Inspect proposals before applying them to stored character data.
  3. Use the Assistant workspace for a conversation outside roleplay. Install a voice engine separately when you want spoken dialogue or voice batches.

Requirements and installation#

Language models, image description and speech use separate compatible components. Choose a model that fits the selected CPU/GPU memory budget. Voice generation does not become available merely because a language model is loaded.

Read Installation and models for setup, the User guide for detailed controls, and Automation and API for the public operation contracts.

pages.title: Installation and models
pages.description: Prepare the runtime, engines and optional models.
pages.html:
Start the application#

Open CyTools_PersonaRP.exe on Windows. If the private runtime is missing, follow the installation steps in Features and installation. Launchers and engine requirements differ by application; do not assume that a copied source folder is a portable installation.

Engines and models#

Language models, image description and speech use separate compatible components. Choose a model that fits the selected CPU/GPU memory budget. Voice generation does not become available merely because a language model is loaded.

Read the licence and source shown for each component before downloading. When access is restricted, open the official model page, obtain access with your account and authenticate locally. Do not paste credentials into generation settings.

Storage#

Keep application data and model weights separate from the application files. Check the selected installation folder and available disk space before starting a large download. Changing a download-cache setting does not move existing models.

Copy the PersonaRP nodes into the custom_nodes folder of a ComfyUI (its folder, its base directory or custom_nodes itself) with a config.json naming this Tool. pages.title: speak_batch_file
pages.description: speakbatch, with files: the list read from file (a script .txt, a CSV .csv/.tsv or a JSON list .json; text or items still work), and personas, the characters the task brings — bundles exported by PersonaRP with their…
pages.html:
speak_batch, with files: the list read from file (a script .txt, a CSV .csv/.tsv or a JSON list .json; text or items still work), and personas, the characters the task brings — bundles exported by PersonaRP with their recordings (sheet, world, stable voices, the per-language ones included). They are copied into the task folder (personnages/) and never into the library, and are looked up before the library; use_library false keeps the task to its own characters. The folder holds the list as given (source.*), the batch as understood (lot.json), one WAV per line in voix/, and resultats.json / resultats.csv. The lines are generated many at a time in one copy of the voice model; with batch_size 0 the number follows the free VRAM, and a batch that does not fit is halved and tried again, so a large GPU is used to the full. A speaker is found by identifier, name, alias or a part of its name no other character has; voice names a stable voice instead, or on top of the character. A line that cannot be spoken is reported and the batch goes on. dry_run checks the list — speakers, voices, languages — before paying for it.

pages.title: speak_batch
pages.description: Speak a list of lines — who says what — into a new task folder of data/batches. The list is sent inline: text holds a script ("Name: line", or "ID | Name: line"), a CSV or a JSON list (format auto recognises them), or items…
pages.html:
Speak a list of lines — who says what — into a new task folder of data/batches. The list is sent inline: text holds a script ("Name: line", or "ID | Name: line"), a CSV or a JSON list (format auto recognises them), or items gives the lines as objects. Every line gets an id — its own, or its number — and its take is named after it. The folder holds the list as given (source.*), the batch as understood (lot.json), one WAV per line in voix/, and resultats.json / resultats.csv. The lines are generated many at a time in one copy of the voice model; with batch_size 0 the number follows the free VRAM, and a batch that does not fit is halved and tried again, so a large GPU is used to the full. A speaker is found by identifier, name, alias or a part of its name no other character has; voice names a stable voice instead, or on top of the character. A line that cannot be spoken is reported and the batch goes on. dry_run checks the list — speakers, voices, languages — before paying for it. resume continues an earlier task without generating its finished lines again. pages.title: translate
pages.description: Translate a stored scene, or a single text, with a language model of your choice. The translation is written beside each turn — the original is never changed — so a scene can carry several languages. Delivery marks such as…
pages.html:
Translate a stored scene, or a single text, with a language model of your choice. The translation is written beside each turn — the original is never changed — so a scene can carry several languages. Delivery marks such as [ton: ...] or [pause: 400ms] are masked before translation and put back afterwards; any the model loses are reported. The answer is constrained to one string per turn. Every request carries the context the words need, never translated itself: the world (genre, tone, setting, the places, factions and terms mentioned first), who speaks and how, where the scene stands, the lines just before in their original words, and your own note in context. A text given together with session_id is translated in the light of that scene, and nothing is stored. The places, factions and terms of the world read the same in every translation: each is rendered once per language, recorded in the world (term_translations; see translation_terms), required in every request, and a line that drops one is asked again once — termsMissed reports what still does.

Command line#

From the application root, use the private Python interpreter. describe and list-operations inspect the public contract.

powershell

MCP#

Configure your MCP client to start the private interpreter with app/tool.py mcp, using the application folder as its working directory. Restart the connection when its exposed operation catalogue changes.

Task files#

Local file inputs accept absolute readable paths and are imported into the task workspace automatically. Export wanted results before finishing the task. Do not rely on temporary paths after task cleanup.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Find a failed installation or operation and preserve useful results.
pages.html:
A model or engine is unavailable#

Check the installation status of the selected backend, not just whether a folder exists. Complete missing downloads, confirm the model format and check its hardware requirements. For restricted models, obtain access on the official site before retrying.

A job fails or takes too long#

Open the application log and read the latest error. Select the relevant lines and copy them, or copy the complete log when reporting a problem. Check source paths, free disk space and RAM/VRAM. Cancel a running job through the application and allow its worker to stop before changing or removing its files.

Keep the output#

Open or export the result before ending an AI task. Temporary task files can be cleaned up when the task finishes. Keep wanted outputs in a separate destination; do not use the Tool’s private job folder as permanent project storage.

pages.title: CyTools PersonaRP sur Google Colab — tâches de voix
pages.description: CyTools PersonaRP sur Google Colab — tâches de voix
pages.html:
CyTools PersonaRP sur Google Colab — tâches de voix#

Ce dossier est un projet à part, fait pour Google Colab et rangé sur votre Google Drive. Il fait dire des listes de répliques par vos personnages, plusieurs à la fois sur le GPU loué, et range tout sur Drive. Il ne contient aucun modèle : l'outil les télécharge lui-même en ligne de commande sur Colab, puis ils sont recopiés sur Drive, où l'outil les relit aux sessions suivantes.

Le SDK CyToolsCore 0.10.1 est public (https://github.com/MrMybal/CyToolsCore, licence MIT) : l'étape Installer le prend sur GitHub, au commit que l'outil fixe dans app/requirements.txt.

Mise en place (une fois)#

  1. Copiez ce dossier entier dans votre Drive, par exemple Mon Drive/CyTools_PersonaRP_Colab.
  2. Dans Drive, ouvrez PersonaRP_Colab.ipynb avec Google Colaboratory.
  3. Exécution › Modifier le type d'exécution : choisissez un GPU (T4, L4, A100…). Le notebook s'adapte à la carte qu'il reçoit.

Déroulé d'une session#

Les cellules du notebook appellent toutes personarp_colab.py en ligne de commande :

Étape Commande Durée indicative
Paramètres chemin du projet, modèles, licence, précision —
Drive et GPU monte Drive, affiche la carte quelques secondes
Installer copie l'outil sur le disque Colab, installe son moteur de voix (PyTorch, Qwen3-TTS) avec l'installeur de l'outil 3 à 5 min, à chaque session
Modèles tool.py invoke install_voice_model : téléchargement par l'outil (révision épinglée, tailles et SHA-256 vérifiés), copie sur Drive vérifiée, puis suppression de la copie locale la première fois seulement (4,5 Go pour le 1.7B Base) ; ensuite « déjà sur Drive »
Essai une réplique sur cette carte ; choisit la précision (bfloat16 sur A100/L4, float16 sur T4, repli en float32 si la prise n'est pas bonne) moins d'une minute
Tâches vérifie chaque tâche sans rien générer : qui dit quoi, avec quelle voix, quel modèle manque quelques secondes
Lancer exécute les tâches selon la liste
État ce qui est installé, sur Drive, et fait —
Rapport écrit resultats/rapport-colab-<date>.json : la carte, le moteur (PyTorch, CUDA), les modèles sur Drive, et le journal de chaque commande de la session (durée, succès, dernières lignes affichées). Sans jeton, sans modèle, sans voix : c'est le fichier à renvoyer pour faire le point quelques secondes

Licences : les modèles ne sont téléchargés que si vous avez coché J_ACCEPTE_LES_LICENCES après avoir lu la licence affichée (Qwen3-TTS : Apache-2.0, page du modèle sur Hugging Face).

Une tâche#

Une tâche est un dossier dans taches/ :

taches/ ma-scene/ liste.csv la liste des répliques (ou .txt, .json) — une seule par dossier personnages/ les personnages exportés par PersonaRP, avec leurs enregistrements valdrenn.zip tache.json facultatif : les réglages de la tâche

Les personnages s'exportent depuis PersonaRP sur votre PC : Bibliothèque › Export et import, cochez Inclure les enregistrements de référence. Le paquet contient la fiche, le monde et toutes les voix stables, y compris celles des autres langues. Colab n'a pas de bibliothèque : une tâche ne parle qu'avec les personnages qu'elle apporte.

La liste a les formats de l'onglet Lots de PersonaRP :

  • CSV : id;personnage;texte;langue (l'id nomme la prise : SC01-05.wav) ;
  • script : SC01-05 | Maëlis: [ton: bas] Le col est fermé. — une ligne par réplique ;
  • JSON : [{"id": "SC01-05", "personnage": "Maëlis", "texte": "…", "langue": "English"}].

tache.json (tout est facultatif) :

{"nom": "ma-scene", "langue": "", "taille_lot": 0, "graine": 42, "precision": "", "bibliotheque": false, "appareil": "cuda"}

langue vide : chaque personnage dans la sienne. taille_lot 0 : taille mesurée sur la carte. precision vide : celle choisie par l'essai.

Les résultats#

Chaque tâche écrit dans resultats/<nom>-<date>/, au fur et à mesure :

personnages/ les personnages que la tâche a apportés source.csv la liste telle que donnée lot.json la tâche telle qu'elle a été comprise voix/ un WAV par réplique, nommé d'après son ID resultats.json pour chaque réplique : ID, texte, fichier, durée, voix et langue, ou l'erreur resultats.csv la même chose pour un tableur

resultats/_taches.json retient ce qui est fait. Si la session Colab s'arrête ou si vous interrompez la cellule, relancez simplement Lancer : la tâche reprend là où elle en était, sans refaire ce qui est déjà écrit sur Drive. Une tâche terminée n'est pas refaite ; pour la refaire, retirez sa ligne de _taches.json.

Plusieurs répliques à la fois#

Les répliques sont générées par lots dans une seule copie du modèle. Un premier lot de 4 mesure ce que coûte une réplique sur la carte, les suivants sont dimensionnés d'après la mémoire libre. Sur une RTX 3090 (24 Go), 16 répliques clonées : 74,7 s une par une, 15,7 s en lots automatiques. Une réplique clonée coûte environ 1,3 Go pendant sa génération.

Ce qui a été vérifié, et ce qui ne l'a pas été#

Vérifié sur Windows (RTX 3090), le 25 septembre 2026 :

  • la fabrication de ce dossier, sans aucun fichier de modèle ;
  • l'outil qui démarre sans interface graphique ni bibliothèque audio ;
  • installer (copie du code, installation légère), etat, taches : la tâche d'exemple signale le modèle manquant et dit quel --modele ajouter ; puis, l'outil lisant ses modèles dans un autre dossier comme il le fera sur Drive, les 10 répliques sont prêtes ;
  • modeles sans accord de licence : l'outil refuse avant tout téléchargement, affiche la licence et sa source, et le jeton du client n'apparaît ni à l'écran ni dans le projet ;
  • la copie vérifiée des modèles (taille et SHA-256, une copie abîmée est détectée) ;
  • les adresses et tailles des 66 fichiers du catalogue de voix sur Hugging Face ;
  • une réplique en float16, la précision d'une T4 : Whisper y retrouve la phrase exacte, comme en bfloat16.

Rien n'a encore tourné sur Colab lui-même : ni l'installation du moteur sous Linux, ni le téléchargement complet d'un modèle par l'outil, ni une tâche sur T4, L4 ou A100. La première session est donc aussi un test ; chaque étape dit clairement ce qui ne va pas.

pages.title: Nodes CyTools PersonaRP pour ComfyUI
pages.description: Nodes CyTools PersonaRP pour ComfyUI
pages.html:
Nodes CyTools PersonaRP pour ComfyUI#

Ces nodes font entrer vos personnages PersonaRP dans ComfyUI : leur apparence pour les modèles d'image, leurs dialogues avec les prompts image et vidéo de la scène, leur voix, et tout le reste de l'outil. Ils sont dans la catégorie CyTools/PersonaRP.

Installation#

Depuis PersonaRP : Bibliothèque › ComfyUI, bouton Installer ici à côté de votre ComfyUI (les installations de Comfy Desktop sont trouvées toutes seules), ou Installer dans ce dossier pour un autre ComfyUI. En ligne de commande, l'opération install_comfyui_nodes fait la même chose. Puis redémarrez ComfyUI.

L'installation copie ce dossier dans custom_nodes/cytools_personarp et écrit config.json, qui dit où est PersonaRP. Réinstaller remplace la copie ; rien d'autre dans ComfyUI n'est touché. Pour les retirer, supprimez simplement ce dossier.

Comment ça marche#

Les nodes n'importent jamais PersonaRP : ComfyUI garde son Python, PersonaRP garde le sien, ses modèles et son moteur de voix. Ils parlent à l'outil par son API locale (adresse 127.0.0.1, jamais le réseau, avec un jeton). Quand un node s'exécute et que PersonaRP ne répond pas, ComfyUI le démarre avec son propre Python, puis l'arrête en se fermant. Ouvrir ComfyUI ne démarre rien : les menus (personnages, voix, modèles) sont lus dans les fichiers de l'outil tant qu'il ne tourne pas.

Le jeton est créé par PersonaRP et rangé dans son dossier data/settings : il n'apparaît dans aucun workflow ni aucun widget.

La barre de progression de ComfyUI suit le travail de l'outil, et le bouton Stop l'annule.

La mémoire graphique#

Une carte de 24 Go ne tient pas à la fois un modèle d'image, un modèle de langage et un modèle de voix. Les nodes qui utilisent le GPU ont deux réglages, activés par défaut :

  • liberer_vram_comfyui : décharge les modèles de ComfyUI avant de demander le travail ;
  • rendre_la_vram_apres : demande à PersonaRP de libérer ses modèles une fois fini.

Désactivez-les pour enchaîner plusieurs nodes PersonaRP sans recharger les modèles.

Les nodes#

Node Entrées Sorties
Personnage un personnage persona_id, nom, apparence, étiquettes visuelles (prêtes pour un prompt), fiche JSON
Dialogue personnage, message, scène (nouvelle, continuer la dernière, continuer une scène donnée, sans mémoire), directive de scène, parler, modèle, appareil, seed réponse, texte parlé, prompt image, prompt vidéo, prompt négatif, directive JSON, audio, session_id
Voix personnage, texte, langue (la configuration de voix par langue de la fiche s'applique), voix stable, seed, appareil audio, fichier (copié dans output/personarp), durée, voix utilisée
Prompts de scène directive JSON (celle du Dialogue), personnage prompt image, prompt vidéo, prompt négatif, résumé
Traduire texte, langue cible, langue source, modèle, personnage et note de contexte facultatifs, session facultative traduction (les marques de jeu [ton: …] restent en place), modèle utilisé
Lire une photo image, langue, modèle de vision apparence, étiquettes visuelles, proposition JSON, modèle utilisé, observation (la description détaillée en anglais dont la fiche est tirée)
Tâche de voix liste (script `ID \ Nom: texte`, CSV ou JSON), nom, langue, taille de lot, précision, paquets de personnages (un chemin par ligne), vérifier seulement
Opération PersonaRP (avancé) n'importe quelle opération de l'outil, paramètres JSON résultat JSON

Les sorties AUDIO se branchent sur les nodes audio de ComfyUI (Save Audio, Preview Audio…), les sorties texte sur n'importe quel encodeur de prompt.

Donner du contexte à la traduction. Une phrase isolée est ambiguë : sans contexte, « le col » a été rendu par « the gate » et « the collar ». Choisissez un personnage : son monde (lieux, termes, ton), sa façon de parler et sa scène en cours accompagnent la demande. Reliez une session_id pour y ajouter les répliques qui précèdent, et écrivez dans contexte ce qu'ils ne disent pas (« au pied d'un col enneigé »). Rien de ce contexte n'est traduit. Avec « (celui de la fiche) » et sans personnage, c'est le modèle de l'assistant qui traduit — souvent un modèle de jeu de rôle ; la sortie modele_utilise dit qui a traduit.

Réglages#

config.json : tool_root (le dossier de PersonaRP), port (8791 par défaut), auto_start. La variable d'environnement PERSONARP_TOOL_ROOT remplace tool_root.

Journal du serveur démarré par ComfyUI : data/logs/comfyui-server.log dans PersonaRP.
pages.text: Nodes CyTools PersonaRP pour ComfyUI # Ces nodes font entrer vos personnages PersonaRP dans ComfyUI : leur apparence pour les modèles d'image, leurs dialogues avec les prompts image et vidéo de la scène, leur voix, et tout le reste de l'outil. Ils sont dans la catégorie CyTools/PersonaRP . Installation # Depuis PersonaRP : Bibliothèque › ComfyUI , bouton Installer ici à côté de votre ComfyUI (les installations de Comfy Desktop sont trouvées toutes seules), ou Installer dans ce dossier pour un autre ComfyUI. En ligne de commande, l'opération install_comfyui_nodes fait la même chose. Puis redémarrez ComfyUI . L'installation copie ce dossier dans custom_nodes/cytools_personarp et écrit config.json , qui dit où est PersonaRP. Réinstaller remplace la copie ; rien d'autre dans ComfyUI n'est touché. Pour les retirer, supprimez simplement ce dossier. Comment ça marche # Les nodes n'importent jamais PersonaRP : ComfyUI garde son Python, PersonaRP garde le sien, ses modèles et son moteur de voix. Ils parlent à l'outil par son API locale (adresse 127.0.0.1 , jamais le réseau, avec un jeton). Quand un node s'exécute et que PersonaRP ne répond pas, ComfyUI le démarre avec son propre Python, puis l'arrête en se fermant. Ouvrir ComfyUI ne démarre rien : les menus (personnages, voix, modèles) sont lus dans les fichiers de l'outil tant qu'il ne tourne pas. Le jeton est créé par PersonaRP et rangé dans son dossier data/settings : il n'apparaît dans aucun workflow ni aucun widget. La barre de progression de ComfyUI suit le travail de l'outil, et le bouton Stop l'annule. La mémoire graphique # Une carte de 24 Go ne tient pas à la fois un modèle d'image, un modèle de langage et un modèle de voix. Les nodes qui utilisent le GPU ont deux réglages, activés par défaut : liberer_vram_comfyui : décharge les modèles de ComfyUI avant de demander le travail ; rendre_la_vram_apres : demande à PersonaRP de libérer ses modèles une fois fini. Désactivez-les pour enchaîner plusieurs nodes PersonaRP sans recharger les modèles. Les nodes # Node Entrées Sorties Personnage un personnage persona_id, nom, apparence, étiquettes visuelles (prêtes pour un prompt), fiche JSON Dialogue personnage, message, scène (nouvelle, continuer la dernière, continuer une scène donnée, sans mémoire), directive de scène, parler, modèle, appareil, seed réponse, texte parlé, prompt image, prompt vidéo, prompt négatif, directive JSON, audio, session_id Voix personnage, texte, langue (la configuration de voix par langue de la fiche s'applique), voix stable, seed, appareil audio, fichier (copié dans output/personarp ), durée, voix utilisée Prompts de scène directive JSON (celle du Dialogue), personnage prompt image, prompt vidéo, prompt négatif, résumé Traduire texte, langue cible, langue source, modèle, personnage et note de contexte facultatifs, session facultative traduction (les marques de jeu [ton: …] restent en place), modèle utilisé Lire une photo image, langue, modèle de vision apparence, étiquettes visuelles, proposition JSON, modèle utilisé, observation (la description détaillée en anglais dont la fiche est tirée) Tâche de voix liste (script `ID \ Nom: texte`, CSV ou JSON), nom, langue, taille de lot, précision, paquets de personnages (un chemin par ligne), vérifier seulement Opération PersonaRP (avancé) n'importe quelle opération de l'outil, paramètres JSON résultat JSON Les sorties AUDIO se branchent sur les nodes audio de ComfyUI (Save Audio, Preview Audio…), les sorties texte sur n'importe quel encodeur de prompt. Donner du contexte à la traduction. Une phrase isolée est ambiguë : sans contexte, « le col » a été rendu par « the gate » et « the collar ». Choisissez un personnage : son monde (lieux, termes, ton), sa façon de parler et sa scène en cours accompagnent la demande. Reliez une session_id pour y ajouter les répliques qui précèdent, et écrivez dans contexte ce qu'ils ne disent pas (« au pied d'un col enneigé »). Rien de ce contexte n'est traduit. Avec « (celui de la fiche) » et sans personnage, c'est le modèle de l'assistant qui traduit — souvent un modèle de jeu de rôle ; la sortie modele_utilise dit qui a traduit. Réglages # config.json : tool_root (le dossier de PersonaRP), port (8791 par défaut), auto_start . La variable d'environnement PERSONARP_TOOL_ROOT remplace tool_root . Journal du serveur démarré par ComfyUI : data/logs/comfyui-server.log dans PersonaRP.

pages.html:
Mondes d'exemple#

Six mondes prêts à jouer, chacun avec ses personnages, leurs relations, leurs voix et un secret à découvrir. Chaque fichier .zip de ce dossier est un paquet d'export ordinaire : un monde, toute sa distribution, et l'enregistrement de référence de chaque voix.

Pour en jouer un : onglet Bibliothèque › Exemples, bouton Importer ce monde. Ou Bibliothèque › Export et import avec le chemin du fichier. L'import est une copie : l'exemple ne change jamais, et un personnage que vous avez déjà n'est jamais écrasé (un second import crée des copies, dont les relations restent liées entre elles).

Les fiches sont complètes : identité, apparence avec étiquettes visuelles, personnalité, façon de parler et exemples de répliques, passé et secrets, situation de départ, mémoire, relations, direction visuelle — et une voix stable par personnage, déjà verrouillée : une prise de 16 à 25 secondes, inventée d'après la description de voix de la fiche et dite avec les mots du personnage. L'import l'ajoute à vos voix ; si une voix du même nom existe déjà chez vous, elle n'est jamais touchée et celle de l'exemple arrive sous un autre identifiant.

Après l'import, chaque voix s'écoute dans l'onglet Voix (« Écouter la prise »). Pour qu'un personnage parle, le modèle de parole 1.7B Base doit être installé (onglet Voix). Pour refaire les voix (autre description, autre texte) : app/build_example_voices.py.

Le modèle de conversation réglé sur les fiches est nymphaea (Nymphaea RP 4B) sur GPU, à installer dans l'onglet Modèles ; changez-le dans Personnages › Modèle si vous en utilisez un autre.

Monde Genre Personnages
Valdrenn — l'Âge des Couronnes Brisées Fantasy épique, quête Maëlis de Corvanne, Brannoc Taillepierre, Ilyenne des Saules, Sire Vasric d'Aubrecourt
Station Méridienne Science-fiction, premier contact Commandante Nadia Okafor-Lenz, ORA, Dr Jun Takeda-Vasseur, Kasimir Rook
Néo-Marseille, 2089 Cyberpunk, polar Lila « Vesper » Anzaldi, Inspecteur Malik Benhadj, Madame Titilayo Oyelaran
Saint-Aubin-des-Brumes, 1887 Horreur gothique Docteure Clémence Vautrin, Père Anselme Keraudren, Élise Morvan
Les Terres Cendrées Post-apocalyptique, western Ada « Sable » Sablière, le Doyen Oskar Venn, Chrome
L'Auberge du Carrefour Fantasy douce, mystère léger Madame Ombeline, Fenouil, Isaure Pluvier

Valdrenn — fantasy épique#

Sept couronnes tiennent en bride la magie sauvage d'un continent ancien ; la septième, qui gouverne les morts, a été brisée il y a mille ans. À l'est, le Roi-Cendre lève les morts qu'on n'a pas nommés et cherche les trois éclats. Maëlis, fille d'aubergiste qui se découvre héritière d'une maison tombée, porte l'un d'eux. Un forgeron taillepierre lié par une dette de sang la protège, une archère sylvaine au sourire las la guide — et le chevalier qui a trahi son père la traque avec une courtoisie terrible.

Un monde dans l'esprit des grandes sagas de fantasy, entièrement original : noms, peuples, lieux et intrigue sont inventés.

Station Méridienne — science-fiction#

En 2291, une station minière aux confins du système de Varun abrite un fragment d'une structure non humaine, l'Écho. Ceux qui dorment près de lui font tous le même rêve. Une commandante épuisée a neuf jours avant l'arrivée d'un croiseur ; l'IA de bord grandit en secret ; un xéno-archéologue ne distingue plus le rêve du réveil ; le pilote qui a trouvé l'Écho veut sa part.

Néo-Marseille, 2089 — cyberpunk#

La mer a monté, la ville s'est reconstruite en hauteur, et les implants se louent au mois. Trois syndicalistes meurent la même nuit d'un arrêt de leur cœur artificiel. Une pêcheuse de données a pêché le code qui les a tués, un inspecteur au bras endetté refuse de classer l'affaire, et une ancienne infirmière tient le bateau-bar où tout le monde se croise.

Saint-Aubin-des-Brumes, 1887 — horreur gothique#

Sur la côte normande, la mer rend parfois ses noyés — froids, doux, pleins des souvenirs des autres. Tous les sept ans, le village lui offre un vivant. Une aliéniste parisienne vient étudier une jeune femme revenue de la mer, qui lui parle avec la voix de son mari disparu, sous le regard d'un curé qui a désigné la dernière offrande.

Les Terres Cendrées — post-apocalyptique#

Soixante et un ans après l'Effondrement, l'eau est la seule monnaie. Le puits de Sainte-Soif meurt ; une caravane part vers l'ouest chercher une Source que tout le monde croit légendaire. Une éclaireuse taciturne, un vieux maître de citerne qui en sait plus qu'il ne le dit, et un androïde agricole déterré qui reconnaît la route sans savoir pourquoi.

L'Auberge du Carrefour — fantasy douce#

Une auberge au bout d'un chemin qui n'existe que sous la pluie, où l'on paie en histoires vraies et où le plancher craque quand on ment. Il pleut depuis neuf jours, et la plus ancienne histoire en bouteille a disparu de la cave. Une aubergiste qui ne se souvient pas d'où elle vient, un renard qui fait le service et mène l'enquête, et une cartographe rongée par le seul mensonge de sa vie.
